rows.title: Math is Mine
rows.objective: Tonight we talk about being a doer of math. A doer of math is anyone who uses math thinking — which is everyone, every day. We also practice estimating: giving a reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful.

rows.title: Math is Exploring and Thinking
rows.objective: Tonight we make sense of a problem, plan a strategy, and use a fraction of a whole number to compare two amounts.

rows.title: Math is In My World
rows.objective: Tonight we draw a real-world money problem as a tape diagram or a table, and then solve it with decimals.

rows.title: Choosing a Tool and Converting Units
rows.objective: Tonight we pick a math tool — a tape diagram, a number line, or a table — and use it to turn a big pile of minutes into hours and minutes.

rows.title: Math is Explaining and Sharing
rows.objective: Tonight we build a math argument. We use volume — the space inside a box — to defend a recommendation with numbers instead of opinions.

rows.title: Defending a Choice with Volume
rows.objective: Tonight we do not just compute — we recommend. We compare two garden bed designs by their volume and then say, in words, which one we would build and why.

rows.title: Math is Finding Patterns
rows.objective: Tonight we look for a pattern, write the pattern rule in words, and use a table of values to check that our answers are reasonable.

rows.title: Using a Pattern Rule to Predict
rows.objective: Tonight we take a pattern that grows by the same amount every time and use it to predict something far in the future — how long a baby whale takes to reach full length.

rows.title: Math is Ours
rows.objective: Tonight we name our problem-solving process: make sense of the problem, choose a representation, make a plan, check progress, and change strategy when stuck.

rows.title: Unit 1 Practice Test
rows.objective: Tonight is practice for the Unit 1 test. Almost every question is dividing with fractions, and the biggest one asks your student to explain a picture — not just write an answer.

rows.title: Pre-Unit 1 · Review
rows.objective: Tonight we review everything from Pre-Unit 1: estimating with reasoning, a fraction of a number, decimal operations, the volume of a box, and pattern rules.

rows.title: Understand Statistical Questions
rows.objective: Tonight we learn to tell the difference between a statistical question and a question with just one fixed answer.

rows.title: Dot Plots and Shape
rows.objective: Tonight we take the answers collected from a statistical question and draw them as a dot plot, then describe the shape the dots make.

rows.title: Represent and Describe Data in a Histogram
rows.objective: Tonight we make a histogram: a bar graph that groups numbers into equal ranges so a big set of data is easy to read.

rows.title: Describing Histogram Shape
rows.objective: Tonight we read a histogram we already know how to build, and say in words what its shape tells us about the data.

rows.title: Describe the Data Using the Median
rows.objective: Tonight we describe a data set using the median — the middle value when the numbers are put in order.

rows.title: Median of an Even Data Set
rows.objective: Tonight we find the median when the data set has an EVEN number of values — so there is no single number sitting in the middle.

rows.title: Represent and Describe Data in a Box Plot
rows.objective: Tonight we build a box plot, a simple picture that shows how data is spread out using five key numbers.

rows.title: Comparing Box Plots
rows.objective: Tonight we put two box plots side by side and compare two groups — first by their centers, then by how spread out they are.

rows.title: Describe Data by Range and Interquartile Range
rows.objective: Tonight we measure how spread out a data set is, using the range and the interquartile range (IQR).

rows.title: Comparing Variability
rows.objective: Tonight we use range and interquartile range together to say which of two groups is more consistent.

rows.title: Divide Multi-Digit Numbers Using an Algorithm
rows.objective: Tonight we divide big numbers by taking away easy chunks, then adding up how many we took out.

rows.title: Long Division in a Real Problem
rows.objective: Tonight we take the long-division steps from Part 1 and use them on a real staffing problem — how many teachers a district has to hire.

rows.title: Divide Decimals Using an Algorithm
rows.objective: Tonight we divide with decimals. The trick is to make the number we divide by a whole number first.

rows.title: Dividing BY a Decimal
rows.objective: Tonight we divide when the DIVISOR is a decimal — like 9.6 ÷ 0.4 — by first turning it into an easier problem with the same answer.

rows.title: Describe Data Using the Mean
rows.objective: Tonight we find the mean of a data set, and we explain the mean two ways: as the fair share and as the balance point of the data.

rows.title: Reaching a Target Mean
rows.objective: Tonight we work the mean backwards: we know the average we WANT, and we find the score still needed to get there.

rows.title: Describe Data by Mean Absolute Deviation
rows.objective: Tonight we find the mean absolute deviation (MAD): the average distance of each number from the mean. It tells us how spread out the data is.

rows.title: Comparing Data Sets Using MAD
rows.objective: Tonight we use MAD — mean absolute deviation — to compare two groups that have the SAME average but do not behave the same at all.

rows.title: Choose Appropriate Measures
rows.objective: Tonight we decide which measure of center, the mean or the median, best describes a "typical" value for a data set.

rows.title: Matching Center and Spread
rows.objective: Tonight we learn which measures go TOGETHER: mean with MAD for symmetric data, median with IQR when there is an outlier.

rows.title: Add and Subtract Decimals
rows.objective: Tonight we add and subtract decimals. The key is to line up the decimal points so the same place values match.

rows.title: Multi-Step Decimal Add and Subtract
rows.objective: Tonight we use decimal adding and subtracting in a running log — a weight that goes down when something is unloaded and up when something is loaded.

rows.title: Multiply Decimals
rows.objective: Tonight we multiply decimals. We multiply like whole numbers first, then count decimal places to put the point in the answer.

rows.title: Multiplying Decimals in Money Problems
rows.objective: Tonight we multiply decimals to find a total cost, and we check whether the answer is reasonable before we trust it.

rows.title: Understand Ratios
rows.objective: Tonight we learn to write a ratio. A ratio is a way to compare two amounts, like 3 cups of apple juice to 2 cups of sparkling water.

rows.title: Equivalent Ratios and Scale Factor
rows.objective: Tonight we make a ratio bigger without changing what it compares. Multiply BOTH quantities by the same number — the scale factor — and you get an equivalent ratio.

rows.title: Understand Rates and Unit Rates
rows.objective: Tonight we connect distance and time. We name both units in a rate, and we use a model to find how long a trip takes.

rows.title: Comparing Unit Prices (Best Buy)
rows.objective: Tonight we write each comparison as a fraction, divide both the top and bottom by the bottom number to find the unit rate in fraction form over 1, and compare to find the best buy.

rows.title: Comparing Unit Rates (Best Value)
rows.objective: Tonight we write each comparison as a fraction with the cost on top and the amount on the bottom, divide both parts by the bottom number to find the unit rate in fraction form over 1, and compare unit rates to pick the better value.

rows.title: Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Tables
rows.objective: Tonight we use a ratio table to make bigger batches of a recipe while keeping it tasting the same.

rows.title: Finding a Missing Value in a Ratio Table
rows.objective: Tonight we find a missing amount in a ratio table by multiplying or dividing BOTH numbers by the same amount — the same move as yesterday, now used to find a missing value up or down.

rows.title: Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Graphs
rows.objective: Tonight we plot the values from a ratio table as points on a grid and see they make a straight line.

rows.title: Reading Points on a Ratio Graph
rows.objective: Tonight we read a ratio graph and say out loud what each point MEANS — especially the point (1, r) and the origin (0, 0).

rows.title: Compare Ratio Relationships
rows.objective: Tonight we compare two cocoa recipes. Which one has more cocoa for the same amount of milk?

rows.title: Comparing Rates with a Benchmark
rows.objective: Tonight we compare two rates by scaling BOTH of them to the same amount — a benchmark — instead of dividing.

rows.title: Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements within the Same System
rows.objective: Tonight we convert one measurement unit into another within the same system, like feet into inches, using a unit ratio.

rows.title: Metric Unit Conversions
rows.objective: Tonight we convert metric units — meters, grams, liters — using powers of ten, and check the answer makes sense.

rows.title: Ratio Reasoning: Convert Measurements Between Systems
rows.objective: Tonight we convert measurements between the customary system (miles, pounds, quarts) and the metric system (kilometers, kilograms, liters).

rows.title: Multi-Step Conversions and Dosage
rows.objective: Tonight we solve problems that need TWO steps in order: convert to the unit the rate uses, and only then apply the rate.

rows.title: Solve Problems with Unit Rates
rows.objective: Tonight we solve real-world rate problems by finding the unit rate — the cost or amount for just 1 — and then using it.

rows.title: Unit Rates in a Buying Decision
rows.objective: Tonight we write comparisons with cost on top and quantity on bottom, divide both parts by the bottom number to find the unit rate in fraction form over 1, and choose the better seller.

rows.title: Equivalent Ratios
rows.objective: Tonight we make and check equivalent ratios — ratios that mean the same thing — using multiplication and division.

rows.title: Scaling a Recipe with Equivalent Ratios
rows.objective: Tonight we scale a recipe up while keeping the ratio the same — and we find the scale factor that makes it work.

rows.title: Convert Measurement Units
rows.objective: Tonight we change one measurement unit into another, like feet into inches, using a conversion factor.

rows.title: Choosing the Direction of a Conversion
rows.objective: Tonight we convert customary units — feet to yards, ounces to pounds — and the whole skill is picking multiply or divide correctly.

rows.title: Understand Percent
rows.objective: Tonight we learn what a percent really means: a comparison to 100. Percent means "per hundred."

rows.title: Percents Greater Than 100%
rows.objective: Tonight we work with percents greater than 100% — what "150% of the goal" or "2.5 times as much" really means.

rows.title: Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
rows.objective: Tonight we write the same value three ways: as a fraction, as a decimal, and as a percent. They all name the same amount.

rows.title: Comparing and Ordering Mixed Forms
rows.objective: Tonight we put fractions, decimals, and percents in order — by first rewriting them all in ONE form.

rows.title: Estimate the Percent of a Number
rows.objective: Tonight we estimate the percent of a number using benchmark percents like 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%.

rows.title: Estimating a Percent of a Number
rows.objective: Tonight we estimate a percent of a number by rounding to friendly values first — and then we explain whether the estimate runs a bit high or a bit low.

rows.title: Find and Compare with Percentages
rows.objective: Tonight we find a percent of a number, like a discount on a price. We change the percent to a decimal and multiply.

rows.title: Comparing with Percents
rows.objective: Tonight we compare two records fairly — two quiz scores out of different totals — by turning each into a percent.

rows.title: Determine the Whole Given the Part and Percent
rows.objective: Tonight we work backwards: when we know a part and the percent that part represents, we find the whole amount it came from.

rows.title: Solving for the Whole with an Equation
rows.objective: Tonight we write a percent equation — part = percent × whole — and solve it for the unknown whole by dividing.

rows.title: Determine the Area of Parallelograms and Rhombuses
rows.objective: Tonight we find the area of a parallelogram. A parallelogram is a slanted four-sided shape, like a leaning rectangle. We use the rule: area = base × height.

rows.title: Area of Rhombuses
rows.objective: Tonight we find the area of a rhombus — and see why the parallelogram formula we learned in Part 1 still works on it.

rows.title: Determine the Area of Triangles
rows.objective: Tonight we find the area of a triangle. A triangle is a shape with three sides. We use the rule: area = ½ × base × height.

rows.title: Missing Measures in Triangles
rows.objective: Tonight we work the triangle area formula BACKWARDS — given the area and one measure, we find the other.

rows.title: Determine the Area of Trapezoids
rows.objective: Tonight we find the area of a trapezoid. A trapezoid is a four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides. Those two sides are the bases, and they have different lengths.

rows.title: The Trapezoid Area Formula
rows.objective: Tonight we use the trapezoid area formula A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h — the shortcut for what we did by cutting shapes apart in Part 1.

rows.title: Apply Area Concepts to Solve Problems
rows.objective: Tonight we find the area of a composite figure — a shape made of two or more simple shapes joined together, like an L-shaped room. We break it apart, find each piece, then add or subtract.

rows.title: Area of Composite Figures
rows.objective: Tonight we find the area of shapes made from other shapes — and decide for each piece whether to ADD it or SUBTRACT it.

rows.title: Determine the Volume of Rectangular Prisms
rows.objective: Tonight we find the volume of a box. Volume is how much space fits inside. We multiply the three edges: length, width, and height.

rows.title: Missing and Fractional Edges
rows.objective: Tonight we work the volume formula backwards to find a missing edge — and we keep fractional edges exact instead of rounding them away.

rows.title: Represent Three-Dimensional Figures in Two Dimensions
rows.objective: Tonight we find the surface area of a box — how much paper it takes to cover the outside. We unfold the box into a flat net and add up all six faces.

rows.title: Reading Nets and Naming Solids
rows.objective: Tonight we look at a flat net and name the solid it folds into — by counting its pieces and their shapes.

rows.title: Determine Surface Area of Prisms
rows.objective: Tonight we find the surface area of prisms, including the wedge-shaped triangular prism. For any prism, we find the area of every face and add them all up.

rows.title: Surface Area of Triangular Prisms
rows.objective: Tonight we find the surface area of a triangular prism — a tent shape — by adding its two triangle ends and its three rectangles.

rows.title: Determine Surface Area of Pyramids
rows.objective: Tonight we find the surface area of a pyramid. We add the area of the flat base plus the area of all the triangle sides that meet at a point on top.

rows.title: Lateral Area of Pyramids
rows.objective: Tonight we find LATERAL area — the slanted faces of a pyramid only, leaving the base out on purpose.

rows.title: Area of Regular Polygons
rows.objective: Tonight we find the area of a regular polygon, like a hexagon (6 sides). We break it into equal triangles, find one triangle's area, then add them all up.

rows.title: Costing a Regular-Polygon Design
rows.objective: Tonight we find the area of a regular polygon by splitting it into identical triangles — and then use that area to price a real job.

rows.title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
rows.objective: Tonight we find the volume of a box even when one edge is a fraction or a decimal, like 1.5. The rule does not change: multiply length × width × height.

rows.title: Comparing Box Volumes to Make a Choice
rows.objective: Tonight we compute the volume of several boxes — fractional edges and all — and use the results to choose one.

rows.title: Division Expressions with Fractions and Whole Numbers
rows.objective: Tonight we model and write division expressions both ways: a whole number divided by a fraction, and a fraction divided by a whole number.

rows.title: 6.1–6.2 · Extra Practice
rows.objective: Tonight we review dividing with fractions from Lessons 6.1 and 6.2 — whole numbers, fractions divided by fractions, and mixed numbers.

rows.title: Mixed Numbers in Fraction Division
rows.objective: Tonight we bring together everything from 6.1 and 6.2: whole numbers, fractions and mixed numbers all divided with Keep, Change, Flip.

rows.title: Dividing a Fraction by a Whole Number
rows.objective: Tonight we divide a fraction BY a whole number — splitting a part into even smaller equal shares.

rows.title: Division Expressions with Fractions and Mixed Numbers
rows.objective: Tonight we divide with mixed numbers like 2 1/2. The trick: turn the mixed number into one simple fraction first, then divide the same way as always.

rows.title: Dividing with Mixed Numbers
rows.objective: Tonight we divide mixed numbers — and the whole trick is turning them into improper fractions BEFORE anything else.

rows.title: Explore Numerical Expressions with Exponents
rows.objective: Tonight we learn what an exponent means. A small raised number tells us how many times a number is used as a factor.

rows.title: Finding the Value of a Power
rows.objective: Tonight we evaluate powers — writing them out as repeated multiplication and finding the value.

rows.title: Write and Evaluate Numerical Expressions with Exponents
rows.objective: Tonight we write one numerical expression for a whole situation and evaluate it using the order of operations, including powers like 2³.

rows.title: Order of Operations with Powers
rows.objective: Tonight we evaluate expressions that mix grouping symbols, powers and arithmetic — in the one order that gives one answer.

rows.title: Write and Evaluate Algebraic Expressions
rows.objective: Tonight we turn words into an algebraic expression, then evaluate it for a given number of students.

rows.title: Evaluating Algebraic Expressions
rows.objective: Tonight we take an algebraic expression, put a number in for the letter, and find its value.

rows.title: Identify Equivalent Algebraic Expressions
rows.objective: Tonight we learn when two expressions are equivalent. Equivalent means they always give the same answer, even when they look different.

rows.title: Testing Equivalence by Substituting
rows.objective: Tonight we TEST whether two expressions are equivalent — by putting the same number into both and comparing.

rows.title: Find Factors and Multiples
rows.objective: Tonight we work with factors and multiples: the greatest common factor (GCF) for splitting things into equal groups, and the least common multiple (LCM) for finding when two repeating things line up.

rows.title: Multiples and the Least Common Multiple
rows.objective: Tonight we find the LEAST COMMON MULTIPLE — the first number two counting patterns land on together.

rows.title: Generate Equivalent Expressions
rows.objective: Tonight we learn math rules called properties. They let us change the order or the grouping of numbers without changing the answer.

rows.title: Expanding and Factoring Expressions
rows.objective: Tonight we do two opposite moves: EXPANDING removes parentheses, and FACTORING puts them back.

rows.title: Divide Whole Numbers by Fractions
rows.objective: Tonight we learn a quick trick to divide a whole number by a fraction. It is called Keep, Change, Flip.

rows.title: Whole Number ÷ Fraction in a Real Problem
rows.objective: Tonight we divide a whole number by a fraction in a real counting problem — how many small bags a big amount fills.

rows.title: Divide Mixed Numbers
rows.objective: Tonight we divide mixed numbers, like 3 1/2. First we change each mixed number into an improper fraction, then we divide with Keep, Change, Flip.

rows.title: Mixed Number ÷ Fraction in a Real Problem
rows.objective: Tonight we divide a mixed number by a fraction to answer a real cutting problem — how many pieces a length gives.

rows.title: Fraction Division Problem Solving
rows.objective: Tonight we solve real-world word problems with fraction division. We read the story, write an equation, solve it, and check that the answer makes sense.

rows.title: Setting Up the Division in a Word Problem
rows.objective: Tonight the hard part is not the arithmetic — it is deciding which number goes FIRST in the division.

rows.title: Least Common Multiple
rows.objective: Tonight we find the least common multiple (LCM) of two numbers. It is the smallest number that both numbers go into.

rows.title: Using the LCM to Buy Matching Packs
rows.objective: Tonight we use the least common multiple to solve a real buying problem — the same number of two things, with none left over.

rows.title: Prime Factorization
rows.objective: Tonight we break a number down into the smaller numbers that multiply to make it. We keep splitting until every piece is a prime number.

rows.title: Finishing a Factor Tree
rows.objective: Tonight we build a factor tree all the way down to primes — and learn to tell when the tree is actually finished.

rows.title: The Distributive Property
rows.objective: Tonight we learn the distributive property. It lets us multiply a number by everything inside the parentheses, one piece at a time.

rows.title: The Distributive Property in a Real Order
rows.objective: Tonight we use the distributive property on a real shopping problem — and show that the factored and expanded forms give the same total.

rows.title: Simplify Algebraic Expressions
rows.objective: Tonight we make an expression shorter by combining like terms. Like terms are terms that have the same variable and exponent.

rows.title: Combining Like Terms, Then Evaluating
rows.objective: Tonight we simplify an expression by combining like terms, then evaluate the simplified version for a given number.

rows.title: Explore Integers and Their Opposites
rows.objective: Tonight we use integers — positive and negative whole numbers — to describe real situations, say what 0 means in each one, and name a number's opposite.

rows.title: Integers in Real Situations
rows.objective: Tonight we write integers for real situations — gains and losses, above and below — and say what ZERO means in each one.

rows.title: Represent Rational Numbers and Their Opposites on the Number Line
rows.objective: Tonight we place rational numbers — fractions and decimals — on a number line, not just integers.

rows.title: Opposites of Rational Numbers
rows.objective: Tonight we find opposites of fractions and decimals — not just whole numbers — and locate both on a number line.

rows.title: Understand Absolute Value of Rational Numbers
rows.objective: Tonight we find the absolute value of a rational number — a whole number, a fraction, or a decimal — as its distance from zero.

rows.title: Absolute Value and Total Distance
rows.objective: Tonight we use absolute value to find the TOTAL distance between two points — including when they sit on opposite sides of zero.

rows.title: Compare and Order Integers and Rational Numbers
rows.objective: Tonight we compare and order integers (positive and negative whole numbers) using a number line.

rows.title: Ordering Integers and Rational Numbers
rows.objective: Tonight we put mixed numbers in order — negatives, fractions and decimals together — using the number line as the judge.

rows.title: Represent Rational Numbers on the Coordinate Plane
rows.objective: Tonight we plot points on a grid called the coordinate plane. We use two numbers, called an ordered pair, to say exactly where a point goes.

rows.title: Reflecting Points Across the Axes
rows.objective: Tonight we reflect points across the x-axis and the y-axis — and see exactly which coordinate changes sign.

rows.title: Determine Distance on the Coordinate Plane
rows.objective: Tonight we find the distance between two points on the grid when they share a row or a column. We use absolute value (distance from zero).

rows.title: Comparing Distances on the Plane
rows.objective: Tonight we find two distances on a grid and compare them — deciding each time whether to add or subtract the absolute values.

rows.title: Represent Polygons on the Coordinate Plane
rows.objective: Tonight we draw a polygon from its vertex coordinates, then use the coordinates to find side lengths, perimeter, and area.

rows.title: Designing Polygons with a Scale
rows.objective: Tonight a grid unit stands for real feet — so we count units, convert to feet, and solve a real design problem.

rows.title: Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants
rows.objective: Tonight we plot points in all four parts of the grid, called quadrants. Now the numbers can be negative, which means left or down.

rows.title: Naming the Quadrant from the Signs
rows.objective: Tonight we name a point's quadrant from its SIGNS alone — without plotting it at all.

rows.title: Reflect Points Across Axes
rows.objective: Tonight we reflect points across the x-axis and the y-axis. A reflection is a flip, like a mirror image.

rows.title: Reflections in a Real Map Problem
rows.objective: Tonight we reflect a point across an axis in a real map problem — and check the distance from the mirror line.

rows.title: Understand Equations and Their Solutions
rows.objective: Tonight we turn a word clue into an equation, and we check whether a value is a solution by substituting it.

rows.title: Writing Equations from Words
rows.objective: Tonight we turn a word problem into an equation — naming the unknown, writing the sentence in symbols, and testing a guess.

rows.title: Write and Solve Equations Using Addition or Subtraction
rows.objective: Tonight we solve an equation that adds or subtracts. To solve means to find the number that makes the equation true.

rows.title: Subtraction Equations
rows.objective: Tonight we solve equations where something was SUBTRACTED from the variable — by adding it back to both sides.

rows.title: Write and Solve Equations Using Multiplication or Division
rows.objective: Tonight we solve equations that multiply or divide. We use the opposite operation to get the letter by itself.

rows.title: Division Equations
rows.objective: Tonight we solve equations where the variable was DIVIDED — by multiplying both sides by the same number.

rows.title: Write and Represent Inequalities
rows.objective: Tonight we write inequalities. An inequality compares two amounts with the signs <, >, ≤, or ≥, when many values are allowed instead of just one.

rows.title: Representing Inequalities on a Number Line
rows.objective: Tonight we show an inequality on a number line — and the open or closed circle tells whether the boundary number counts.

rows.title: Understand Inequalities and Their Solutions
rows.objective: Tonight we graph an inequality on a number line. We draw a circle at the boundary number and shade the side that works.

rows.title: Testing Solutions to Inequalities
rows.objective: Tonight we TEST values in an inequality — including the boundary number — and then graph what we found.

rows.title: Solve and Graph Inequalities
rows.objective: Tonight we solve an inequality and then graph it. We get the letter alone the same way as an equation, but the answer is a range of values.

rows.title: Solving, Then Graphing an Inequality
rows.objective: Tonight we SOLVE an inequality first, then graph its solution set — and the shading follows the SOLVED symbol, not the original.

rows.title: Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving
rows.objective: Tonight we read a word problem and decide whether to model it with an equation or an inequality, then solve it and check that the answer makes sense.

rows.title: Choosing an Equation or an Inequality
rows.objective: Tonight the decision comes first: does this situation give ONE exact value, or a LIMIT? That picks equation or inequality.

rows.title: Explore Relationships Between Two Variables
rows.objective: Tonight we look at two quantities that change together and decide which one is the independent variable and which is the dependent variable.

rows.title: Tables of Values
rows.objective: Tonight we build a table of values — input in the first column, output in the second — and find the rule connecting them.

rows.title: Analyze Graphs of Relationships Between Two Variables
rows.objective: Tonight we turn a table into a graph. Each row of the table becomes one point on the coordinate plane.

rows.title: Analyzing a Graph
rows.objective: Tonight we read a relationship off a graph — its rate of change, its unit rate — and use it to predict a value we cannot see.

rows.title: Write Equations to Represent Relationships Between Two Variables
rows.objective: Tonight we write an equation from a table or a graph, so two letters can describe the whole relationship.

rows.title: Writing Equations from Situations
rows.objective: Tonight we turn a real situation into an equation — spotting the rate that MULTIPLIES and any starting amount that ADDS.

rows.title: Apply Two-Variable Relationships to Solve Problems
rows.objective: Tonight we use an equation to answer a real question: write it, substitute the number we know, solve, and explain what the answer means.

rows.title: Working Backward to a Goal
rows.objective: Tonight we start from the GOAL and work backward. Put the target in place of the output, then undo the operations one at a time to find the input that reaches it.

rows.title: Math is Everywhere
rows.objective: Tonight we look for math outside of school — in jobs like being a chef, in hobbies like gardening, and around our own house.

rows.title: Modeling a Real Household Question
rows.objective: Tonight we use math on something at home — turning a small daily habit into a year's worth of numbers.

rows.title: Math is Beauty
rows.objective: Tonight we use bilateral symmetry — two sides that are mirror images — to describe shapes in nature and in things people build.

rows.title: Math is Playful
rows.objective: Tonight we play with the Tower of Hanoi puzzle and look for a pattern that predicts the number of moves.

rows.title: Finding the Rule in a Puzzle
rows.objective: Tonight we solve a puzzle by starting SMALL — tracing simple cases until a pattern rule appears.

rows.title: Math is Ingenuity
rows.objective: Tonight we use ratios to explain how bicycle gears work — why one turn of the pedals can spin the wheel more than once.

rows.title: Math is Boundless
rows.objective: Tonight we design with repetition and rhythm, and we use the pattern unit — the part that repeats — to predict what comes next.

rows.title: Math is Mine
rows.objective: Tonight we look back at the very first lesson of the year and describe how our math story has grown.
